ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a series-pass regulated power supply. At the upper left is an unregulated input marked 15V (UR), which goes through the upper transistor Q1 to the output node on the right. The output node on the right is labeled Vout, and has a 10Ω load resistor connected to ground. The output node is also connected to a voltage divider made of 12kΩ and 24kΩ in series, the lower end of the 24kΩ is grounded, and the midpoint of the 12kΩ and 24kΩ is fed back to the negative input terminal of the operational amplifier. On the left there is a 1kΩ resistor connected from the input terminal to a reference node, this node is connected to ground through a Zener diode marked 6V, and is connected to the positive input terminal of the operational amplifier; the operational amplifier output drives Q1. Reasoning: During regulation, the feedback node voltage equals the 6V Zener reference voltage. The lower resistor in the voltage divider is 24kΩ, and the total resistance is 12kΩ + 24kΩ = 36kΩ, so the feedback voltage is Vout·24/36. Setting 6 = Vout·24/(12+24) gives Vout = 9V. The output load current is 9V/10Ω = 0.9A; the voltage-divider current is 9V/36kΩ, which is very small, and since Vout is kept unchanged by regulation, these output-side currents remain unchanged. Initially, the voltage drop across Q1 is 15V - 9V = 6V, so the initial power dissipation is proportional to 6V multiplied by the constant output-side current. After the unregulated input increases by 20%, UR = 15V × 1.2 = 18V; the regulated output is still 9V, and the output-side current is still the same. At this time, the voltage drop across Q1 is 18V - 9V = 9V. The power dissipation ratio is 9/6 = 1.5, so the Q1 power dissipation becomes 150% of the original, that is, increases by 50%.

raw_record.question_text:
A regulated power supply has an unregulated input (UR) of 15 Volts and generates a regulated output \(V_{out}\). Use the component values shown in the figure.

The ground is shown by the symbol \(\nabla\). If the unregulated voltage increases by 20%, by what percentage does the power dissipation across transistor Q1 change?

method.method_draft: First describe the image components and connections. Set the feedback node voltage equal to the 6 V zener reference. Since the lower divider resistor is 24 kΩ and the total divider is 36 kΩ, solve 6 = Vout·24/(12+24) to get Vout = 9 V. Compute the load current 9/10 = 0.9 A and, if desired, add the small divider current 9/36 kΩ; this current remains constant because Vout is regulated. Initial transistor voltage drop is 15 - 9 = 6 V, so initial Q1 power is 6 times the constant output-side current. A 20% increase makes UR = 18 V, while Vout and current stay at 9 V and the same current, so the new Q1 drop is 18 - 9 = 9 V. The power ratio is 9/6 = 1.5, meaning the dissipation increases by 50%.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A regulated power supply has an unregulated input (UR) of 15 Volts and generates a regulated output \(V_{out}\). Use the component values shown in the figure. The ground is shown by the symbol \(\nabla\). If the unregulated voltage increases by 20%, by what percentage does the power dissipation across transistor Q1 change?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a series-pass regulated power supply. At the upper left is an unregulated input marked 15V (UR), which goes through the upper transistor Q1 to the output node on the right. The output node on the right is labeled Vout, and has a 10Ω load resistor connected to ground. The output node is also connected to a voltage divider made of 12kΩ and 24kΩ in series, the lower end of the 24kΩ is grounded, and the midpoint of the 12kΩ and 24kΩ is fed back to the negative input terminal of the operational amplifier. On the left there is a 1kΩ resistor connected from the input terminal to a reference node, this node is connected to ground through a Zener diode marked 6V, and is connected to the positive input terminal of the operational amplifier; the operational amplifier output drives Q1. Reasoning: During regulation, the feedback node voltage equals the 6V Zener reference voltage. The lower resistor in the voltage divider is 24kΩ, and the total resistance is 12kΩ + 24kΩ = 36kΩ, so the feedback voltage is Vout·24/36. Setting 6 = Vout·24/(12+24) gives Vout = 9V. The output load current is 9V/10Ω = 0.9A; the voltage-divider current is 9V/36kΩ, which is very small, and since Vout is kept unchanged by regulation, these output-side currents remain unchanged. Initially, the voltage drop across Q1 is 15V - 9V = 6V, so the initial power dissipation is proportional to 6V multiplied by the constant output-side current. After the unregulated input increases by 20%, UR = 15V × 1.2 = 18V; the regulated output is still 9V, and the output-side current is still the same. At this time, the voltage drop across Q1 is 18V - 9V = 9V. The power dissipation ratio is 9/6 = 1.5, so the Q1 power dissipation becomes 150% of the original, that is, increases by 50%.
